label: Retinue men-at-arms
summary: The game concept Retinue Men-at-Arms: special men-at-arms unlocked by some accolade types.
details: They are unlocked by an acclaimed knight with progress in a matching tourney participant track or a matching commander trait. label: Retract

Vanilla uses it in concept texts about a liege's powers over vassals and in a notice for a diarch.

label: Rightful liege
summary: The game concept Rightful Liege: the ruler holding the de jure title directly above a vassal's primary title.
details: A vassal who is not under their rightful liege gives less taxes and levies and has an opinion penalty towards their liege; holding a higher title of the same de jure line softens this. Dukes of an empire's de jure lands serving the emperor directly still give everything. In a text, `[rightful_liege|E]` shows "Rightful Liege" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in many vassal texts.

label: Rite
summary: The game concept Rite: a branch of a faith, with its own local religious practices, head of rite, counties and followers.
details: Every faith has a mainline rite and may grow more. A rite is defined by its core tenets and doctrines; the more it departs from what the faith (through its mainline rite) allows, the higher its divergence, and at 100 divergence it breaks away as a new faith. Only the head of rite may edit it. In a text, `[rite|E]` shows "Rite" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it very often.

label: Divergence
summary: The game concept Divergence: how far a rite's core tenets and doctrines have drifted from its parent faith.
details: Adopting tenets the faith prohibits as core tenets raises it. High divergence lowers the parent faith's fervor and makes heresy outbreaks more common; a rite that reaches 100 is declared a heresy and becomes a new faith. In a text, `[rite_divergence|E]` shows "Divergence" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in texts that lower a rite's divergence.

In a text, `[ritsuryo_government|E]` shows "Ritsuryō Government" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the Japanese bureaucracy concept's text.

label: Scheme phase length
summary: The game concept Scheme Phase Length: how many days a scheme needs to finish one of its phases.
details: Shorter is better, because the scheme then advances faster. It depends on the schemer's skill, their agents and spymaster, and for hostile schemes on the spymaster's Support Schemes task. In a text, `[scheme_speed|E]` shows "Scheme Phase Length" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Phase length icon
summary: The icon of the game concept Scheme Phase Length (how many days a scheme needs for one phase).
details: Its text is only the phase-length icon (`@scheme_phase_duration_icon!`). Vanilla writes `[scheme_speed_i]` in front of agent focus and agent slot lines.

label: Phase length
summary: Another name of the game concept Scheme Phase Length (the days a scheme needs for one phase), shown as "Phase Length".
details: In a text, `[scheme_speed_single|E]` shows "Phase Length" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the spymaster's Support Schemes task and in the concept texts on agents and scheme phases.

label: Scheme success chance
summary: The game concept Scheme Success Chance: how likely a scheme is to succeed when it is carried out.
details: It grows over time, from the schemer's matching skill and the agents, and is capped by the scheme's potential. No scheme goes above 95% except contract schemes. In a text, `[scheme_success_chance|E]` shows "Scheme Success Chance" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Scheme target
summary: The game concept Scheme Target: the character a scheme is aimed at by its owner, such as the would-be victim of a murder.
details: In a text, `[scheme_target|E]` shows "Scheme Target" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in secrecy texts and in the concept texts on scheme owners and personal schemes.

label: Scheme target
summary: Another name of the game concept Scheme Target (the character a scheme is aimed at), shown as the single word "Target".
details: In a text, `[scheme_target_target|E]` shows "Target" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in concept texts about extra measures and failed murders.

label: Scheme target's
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Scheme Target (the character a scheme is aimed at).
details: Despite the plural-looking name, its text is "Scheme Target's": `[scheme_targets|E] virtues` reads "Scheme Target's virtues", linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it that way in movement-power scheme texts.

label: Scheme owner
summary: Another name of the game concept Scheme Owner: the character running a scheme against its target, such as the would-be killer in a murder.
details: In a text, `[schemer|E]` shows "Schemer" linked to the concept's explanation. The vanilla lines given all write `[schemer.GetTitledFirstName]` and the like in a story cycle's texts: there `schemer` most likely names a character saved under that name, not this concept.

label: Schemes
summary: The plural of the game concept Scheme: a long-term attempt by a character to change the world around them.
details: Schemes can target characters, titles, cultures and faiths, and are personal, hostile, political or contract schemes. In a text, `[schemes|E]` shows "Schemes" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Scheming
summary: Another name of the game concept Scheme (a long-term attempt to affect the world), shown as the word "Scheming".
details: In a text, `[scheming|E]` shows "Scheming" linked to the Scheme explanation. Vanilla uses it in interaction texts such as "You are already scheming against …".

label: Schism
summary: The game concept Schism: the Great Schism, when the united Christian faith splits along its Roman and Greek rites into Catholic and Orthodox.
details: It looms in certain chapters of the Christian Church situation, and rulers must take a side; unless decisions mend or force the split, it becomes permanent when the chapter ends. In a text, `[schism|E]` shows "Schism" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it for the schism's progress.

label: Schisms
summary: The plural of the game concept Schism (the Great Schism of the Christian faith into Catholic and Orthodox).
details: In a text, `[schisms|E]` shows "Schisms" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Screen
summary: The game concept Screen: an army value that lowers the casualties a defeated army takes in the aftermath of a battle.
details: The losing army's casualties are reduced by its combined Screen. In a text, `[screen|E]` shows "Screen" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in men-at-arms stats and descriptions.

label: Seal of investiture
summary: The game concept Seal of Investiture: a document and symbol showing that a tributary is a loyal, favoured tributary of the Chinese emperor.
details: It can be granted to tributaries with high imperial grace at the end of a successful tribute mission. In a text, `[seal_of_investiture|E]` shows "Seal of Investiture" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla also uses it in the seal artifact's description.

label: Seasonal prediction
summary: The game concept Seasonal Prediction: a skilled court astrologer's forecast of the next steppe season in a region.
details: It helps the astrologer's liege plan ahead. In a text, `[seasonal_prediction|E]` shows "Seasonal Prediction" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in the Great Steppe window.

label: Secrecy
summary: The game concept Secrecy: how likely a hostile scheme is to stay hidden from its target.
details: A scheme starts with a grace period in which it cannot be found; after that it risks discovery every month through a breach. Agents strongly affect it. In a text, `[secrecy|E]` shows "Secrecy" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Secrecy grace
summary: The game concept Grace: the opening period of a scheme, a few months long, in which it cannot be discovered.
details: After the grace period a scheme may be discovered each month, causing a breach; the monthly chance is much lower than at execution but checked far more often. In a text, `[secrecy_grace|E]` shows "Grace" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in the scheme window for the months left.

label: Secrecy icon
summary: The icon of the game concept Secrecy (how likely a hostile scheme stays hidden).
details: Its text is only the secrecy icon (`@scheme_secrecy_icon!`). Vanilla writes `[secrecy_i]` in front of agent focus and agent slot lines that improve secrecy.

label: Secret
summary: The game concept Secret: something a character wants hidden because it is embarrassing, immoral or criminal.
details: Secrets can be found with the spymaster's Find Secrets task; knowing one lets you blackmail the character for a hook. In a text, `[secret|E]` shows "Secret" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Secret scheme
summary: The game concept Secret Scheme: a scheme that advances without its target knowing.
details: If it is discovered, its success chance drops and the owner is more likely to be exposed when it executes; its agents may be discovered too. In a text, `[secret_scheme|E]` shows "Secret Scheme" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Secret scheme
summary: Another name of the game concept Secret Scheme (a scheme hidden from its target), shown as the single word "Secret".
details: In a text, `[secret_scheme_single|E]` shows "Secret" linked to the Secret Scheme explanation. Vanilla uses it in scheme descriptions ("it is not Secret and does not use agents").

label: Secret schemes
summary: The plural of the game concept Secret Scheme (a scheme that advances without its target knowing).
details: In a text, `[secret_schemes|E]` shows "Secret Schemes" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in the scheme window's list of discovered schemes.

label: Secrets
summary: The plural of the game concept Secret (something a character wants hidden because it is embarrassing, immoral or criminal).
details: In a text, `[secrets|E]` shows "Secrets" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in achievements and AI personality texts.

label: Secular
summary: Another name of the game concept Secular Ruler (a ruler whose government is not a religious one), shown as the word "Secular".
details: In a text, `[secular|E]` shows "Secular" linked to the Secular Ruler explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Secular obligations
summary: The game concept Secular Obligations: the rule for how much income from church holdings goes to the local secular ruler.
details: It comes in a personal and a fixed type, set by the Christian Church situation; in some chapters secular rulers also gain local power over the Church. In a text, `[secular_obligations|E]` shows "Secular Obligations" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Secular opinion
summary: The game concept Secular Opinion: a kind of opinion that applies to every character who is not clergy.
details: In a text, `[secular_opinion|E]` shows "Secular Opinion" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in trait opinion lines.

label: Secular ruler
summary: The game concept Secular Ruler: a ruler whose government form is not a religious one.
details: In a text, `[secular_ruler|E]` shows "Secular Ruler" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it as the link in lease-expense and Christian Church texts. A line such as `[secular_ruler.GetTitledFirstNamePossessive]` most likely uses a saved character of the same name, not this concept.

label: Secular rulers
summary: The plural of the game concept Secular Ruler (a ruler whose government is not religious).
details: In a text, `[secular_rulers|E]` shows "Secular Rulers" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in the Christian Church situation's parameters.

label: Iberian foothold
summary: The game concept Iberian Foothold: a decision that lets a ruler not involved in the Iberian struggle end it.
details: In a text, `[secure_iberian_foothold_decision|E]` shows the decision's name, "Iberian Foothold", linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in the struggle parameter that unlocks the decision.

label: Seize peripheral duchy
summary: The game concept Seize Peripheral Duchy: a casus belli (war reason) for rulers bordering a realm with a bureaucratic government.
details: It lets the attacker take a neighbouring duchy that lies outside the de jure hierarchy of the defender's capital. In a text, `[seize_peripheral_duchy|E]` shows "Seize Peripheral Duchy" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it as the casus belli's name.

label: Sell titles
summary: Another name of the game concept Sell Titles Decision: a decision to sell purely symbolic minor titles, giving gold for prestige.
details: In a text, `[sell_titles|E]` shows "Sell Titles" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in an effect text that allows the decision.

label: Sell titles decision
summary: The game concept Sell Titles Decision: a decision to sell trivial, purely symbolic titles, gaining gold and paying with prestige.
details: In a text, `[sell_titles_decision|E]` shows "Sell Titles Decision" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in a struggle parameter that unlocks it for kings and emperors.

label: Send gift
summary: Another name of the game concept Gift: sending gold to another character to raise their opinion of you.
details: Greedier recipients need more gold but give more opinion, and higher diplomacy gives more opinion. In a text, `[send_gift|E]` shows "Send Gift" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it for bonuses to gift cost and opinion gain.

label: Settlement issue
summary: The game concept Settlement Issue: a task a nomad ruler gets after migrating to new lands, a chance to settle conflicts and raise county control there.
details: Such issues keep coming for the first years after the migration while the county's control (how firmly the holder controls it) stays low. In a text, `[settlement_issue|E]` shows "Settlement Issue" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Settlement issue tier
summary: The game concept Settlement Issue Tier: the level of a settlement issue, showing how big its rewards are when solved.
details: A higher tier usually gives more rewards on top of the county control. In a text, `[settlement_issue_tier|E]` shows "Settlement Issue Tier" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Sexual orientation
summary: The game concept Sexual Orientation: which other characters a character can be attracted to.
details: It does not limit whom they can marry, but a couple's fertility may drop when a spouse does not match the other's preference. In a text, `[sexuality|E]` shows "Sexual Orientation" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Share power
summary: Another name of the game concept Power Sharing: a ruler sharing some authority with a vassal or courtier, who becomes their diarch.
details: The ruler can set mandates for the diarch, the diarch has special powers, and the scales of power show who holds more authority. In a text, `[share_power|E]` shows "Share Power" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Sharing power
summary: Another name of the game concept Power Sharing (a ruler sharing authority with a diarch), shown as "Sharing Power".
details: In a text, `[sharing_power|E]` shows "Sharing Power" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in court position and vizier texts.

label: Shōen
summary: Another name of the game concept Japanese Manor: a domicile held by the house heads of notable noble families in Japanese realms, a private landholding not tied to any landed title.
details: Manor buildings can be built there. In a text, `[shoen|E]` shows "Shōen" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Shōgun
summary: The game concept Shōgun: the de facto ruler of all Japan, who rules in the emperor's place with a hereditary succession.
details: In a text, `[shogun|E]` shows "Shōgun" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it as the link in a decision text about the Shōgunate; its event texts write `[shogun.GetName]` and the like, where `shogun` most likely names a saved character, not this concept.

label: Shōgun's
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Shōgun (the de facto hereditary ruler of all Japan).
details: In a text, `[shogun_possessive|E]` shows "Shōgun's" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses it.

label: Short reign
summary: The game concept Short Reign: an opinion penalty everyone in a realm has toward a new liege, which fades over time.
details: Its counterpart is the Long Reign bonus, which grows the longer a liege rules. In a text, `[short_reign|E]` shows "Short Reign" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Shunned
summary: The game concept Shunned: behaviour that a rite's doctrines mark as disapproved, and depending on the doctrine also as criminal.
details: A character caught doing what their rite shuns loses a piety level and gains a matching fame trait, disliked by everyone whose rite shuns or forbids it. In a text, `[shunned|E]` shows "Shunned" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Sick
summary: Another name of the game concept Illness (negative traits that lower a character's health), shown as the word "Sick".
details: Illnesses last for different times and differ greatly in how deadly they are. In a text, `[sick|E]` shows "Sick" linked to the Illness explanation; vanilla uses it that way in a trait text. A line such as `[sick.GetHerHis]` in an event most likely uses a saved character of the same name, not this concept.

label: Sickness
summary: Another name of the game concept Illness (negative traits that lower a character's health), shown as the word "Sickness".
details: In a text, `[sickness|E]` shows "Sickness" linked to the Illness explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Siege
summary: The game concept Siege: an army surrounding a fortified holding to starve it into submission so it can be occupied.
details: A siege starts by itself when an army stands still at a hostile fortified holding and outnumbers its garrison. Once the walls are breached the besiegers can assault. In a text, `[siege|E]` shows "Siege" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Siege progress
summary: The game concept Siege Progress: how close a siege is to completion; when it is full, the holding is occupied.
details: The amount needed depends on the fort level and how well the garrison is manned. Progress is gained daily, changed by siege events, and raised by siege weapons. In a text, `[siege_progress|E]` shows "Siege Progress" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Siege weapon
summary: The game concept Siege Weapon: men-at-arms built only for sieges, which speed them up by adding siege progress.
details: They do nothing in battles and only work against holdings up to a certain fort level. In a text, `[siege_weapon|E]` shows "Siege Weapon" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Siege weapons
summary: The plural of the game concept Siege Weapon (men-at-arms that only speed up sieges).
details: In a text, `[siege_weapons|E]` shows "Siege Weapons" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in the concept texts on breaches and fort levels.

label: Sieges
summary: The plural of the game concept Siege (an army surrounding a fortified holding to occupy it).
details: In a text, `[sieges|E]` shows "Sieges" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Silk Road
summary: Another name of the game concept Silk Road: the network of trade routes linking distant lands for gold, goods and ideas.
details: Different levels of access give gold bonuses and may unlock exotic innovations. In a text, `[silk_road|E]` shows "Silk Road" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in building, message filter and innovation texts.

label: Silk Road innovation
summary: The game concept Silk Road Innovation: innovations that travel westwards along the Silk Road.
details: Every few years an innovation discovered by Han culture enters the China region of the Silk Road, and the others move one step further west. In a text, `[silk_road_innovation|E]` shows "Silk Road Innovation" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Silk Road icon
summary: The icon of the game concept Silk Road Innovation (innovations that travel west along the Silk Road).
details: Its text is only the Silk Road icon (`@silk_road_icon!`); `[silk_road_innovation_i|E]` shows the icon linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the culture window.

label: Silk Road innovation
summary: A short name of the game concept Silk Road Innovation (innovations that travel west along the Silk Road), shown as just "Silk Road".
details: In a text, `[silk_road_innovation_short|E]` shows "Silk Road" linked to the Silk Road Innovation explanation. Vanilla uses it after the icon in the icon-and-name form.

label: Silk Road innovation
summary: The game concept Silk Road Innovation shown as the Silk Road icon followed by the short name "Silk Road".
details: Its text is `@silk_road_icon! [silk_road_innovation_short|E]`, so the icon and the linked short name appear together. No vanilla text uses it.
